title: feat(plugin-grid): server-side grid grouping — group headers from the query, rows paged per group (objectui#7189)
body:
Fixes #7189

Clause-②: yes — measured on this branch, where the claim reads `no`. No metadata or schema key moves (`GroupingConfig` is unchanged), but published TypeScript surface does: `DataSource` in `@object-ui/types` gains the optional member `queryGroupHeaders`, `ObjectStackAdapter` implements it, and `@object-ui/plugin-grid`'s exported `GroupEntry` (new `count`, `keyValues`), `AggregationResult.value` (now `number | null`) and `useGroupedData` (optional fifth argument) change shape. The seat corrects the claim line.

## What this does

Maintainer ruling A on this card: grouping on a list view is server-side. The set of groups and every number in a group header are properties of the query, not of the fetched page; rows inside a group are paged. This PR is the objectui half, on top of the spec half (objectstack#14556) and the platform half (objectstack#15330).

- **Transport (`@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/data-objectstack`).** `DataSource.queryGroupHeaders(resource, query)` answers the header query `compileListViewGroupQuery` compiles. Presence is the capability. The ObjectStack adapter posts it verbatim to the existing `POST /data/:object/query` door and answers its `records`; it never degrades (a refusal throws with the server's code and status; a body without `records` is refused, not read as zero groups). The adapter already had an undeclared spec-shape branch on `aggregate()`; it was not reused because `AggregateParams` does not declare that shape and the other adapters would answer it with garbage, so a new optional member is the smallest honest addition.
- **Grid (`@object-ui/plugin-grid`).** A grouped grid that fetches its own rows from such a source no longer fetches a flat window. It asks one compiled header query per grouping level (outer headers are their own level's numbers; `avg` / `count_distinct` do not fold) and pages each open group's rows with that group's compiled row query (`compileListViewGroupRowsQuery`: view filter AND group key, `limit` / `offset` per group). Each group larger than the page gets its own pager. A collapsed group costs no row query. `aggregations` ride the header query (mapped onto the spec's column summaries and read back with `deriveColumnSummary`). A reference-typed grouping key (a raw id on the wire) is labelled from the referenced record. The view filter is lowered once to a `FilterCondition` (`parseFilterAST`) and handed to both compilers, so header numbers and rows answer the same question; a filter that does not lower is refused, never dropped. Grouping keys the principal may not read are not sent as keys.
- **`useServerPagination`.** The grouped exclusion goes for a server-grouped grid: its rows are paged by the server (per group) and its sort is the server's.
- **`useGroupedData`.** With the server's header rows it builds the group tree from them and never buckets `data`. Without them it still groups rows the grid holds.
- **`Partial` marker.** Retired where counts are server-true: a server-grouped grid never renders it. See the open question below for the one shape that still reaches it.
- **ListView (`@object-ui/plugin-list`).** The console mounts the grid through `ListView`, which fetched one window and handed it down as `data`, so the grid could only group a page (and the #7226 marker never fired on that path, because no total was handed down for grouped grids). When the data source can answer the header query, `ListView` now hands a grouped grid NO rows, passes it the effective filter (authored + toolbar + chips, the same value the self-querying views get), and draws no record-count bar over it. While a toolbar search is active it keeps hosting the window as before (see the out-of-scope finding: the aggregate door drops `search`). This is outside the claim's named file surface; it is where the page-scoped rows actually came from in the console.

## Step zero, measured before any grid code (G0)

The installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 (read from this worktree's `node_modules`) compiled the header query for the 186-row, five-unit fixture, posted through objectstack's real `RestServer` route over `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` + `ObjectQL` + in-memory SQLite, from a throwaway objectstack worktree at `origin/main` `d3958bac` (removed afterwards):

- header query `{"groupBy":["business_unit"],"aggregations":[{"function":"count","alias":"count"},...]}` answered five rows 86 / 61 / 31 / 7 / 1 in both the contiguous and the interleaved object, `total: 5`;
- the compiled row query for the 86-row group paged 50 + 36 (`total: 86` on both pages), 86 distinct ids;
- control on the same door: grouping the first 100 stored rows gives 86 / 14 (contiguous) and 31 / 31 / 30 / 7 / 1 (interleaved).

Then end to end with this branch's BUILT adapter and the installed `@objectstack/client`, wired by a fetch shim into the same real routes: `queryGroupHeaders` answered 86 / 61 / 31 / 7 / 1, and paging every group through `adapter.find` with the compiled row query reached all 186 rows (86 as 50 + 36). The empty group (nine rows with a NULL key) was reached through the `is_null` predicate, and a `status = done` view filter moved header numbers and rows together (28 / 20 / 10 / 2, one unit gone).

## Pins

- `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/serverGrouping-7189.test.tsx` (11): five headers 86 / 61 / 31 / 7 / 1 and no marker in both row orders; the header query equals the spec compiler's output and no flat window is fetched; the 86-row group shows 86 rows under a 100-row window; under a 50-row window it pages 50 then 36 (union 86); all 186 rows reachable through the group pagers; a per-group `sum` is the query's; a collapsed group costs no row query; two-level headers come from one query per depth; a lookup key is labelled from the referenced record; CONTROL: a source without the header query still renders 86 / 14 with the marker.
- `packages/data-objectstack/src/queryGroupHeaders-7189.test.ts` (4): verbatim body to the door, records answered, refusal without `records`, no fallback on a 400.
- `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.groupedGridOwnsFetch-7189.test.tsx` (4): grouped grid gets no rows and the effective filter, no record-count bar; controls for a source without the header query and for an ungrouped grid.
- `groupedPartialDisclosure-7189.test.tsx` is NOT retired: its data sources declare no `queryGroupHeaders`, so it now pins the fallback (header updated to say so). `groupedPagination.test.tsx` needed no rewrite (inline rows).

**Ablation** (prediction written before the run): forcing `serverGroupedFetch` to false in `ObjectGrid.tsx` turned `serverGrouping-7189.test.tsx` to exactly `Tests 10 failed | 1 passed (11)` as predicted, the one pass being the control. Mutation landed on disk through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `957bad075ca7` to `6324d33743e9`), restored and proven by blob equal to HEAD and empty `git diff HEAD`. No build stands between edit and run: the test imports `../ObjectGrid` and the root vitest config aliases `@object-ui/plugin-grid` to `src`. A first attempt was refused by the tool before running (the replacement contained the anchor), so it measured nothing.

A live browser run of the console against a running backend was not made; the in-process route probe above stands in for it.

## Semver

`minor` on types, data-objectstack, plugin-grid and plugin-list (fixed group, no `major` per this repo's policy); the breaking semantics are stated in the changeset. The floors of plugin-grid and data-objectstack move to `@objectstack/spec` `^17.4.0`, the first release carrying the compilers. The pending `.changeset/7189-grouped-grid-partial-disclosure.md` carries two sentences this makes false: "That is a correct implementation of client-side grouping and is **unchanged** here" and "Server-side grouping — the durable fix — is deliberately NOT part of this ... nothing here builds toward it or changes the fetch." Following this repo's precedent for a pending changeset a later change makes false, both halves are done: the new changeset says it supersedes that paragraph, and a dated note (2026-09-28, naming objectui#7189 and this PR) is appended at the end of `.changeset/7189-grouped-grid-partial-disclosure.md` correcting those sentences and the one before them (that `useGroupedData` buckets the rows the browser already holds). The existing paragraphs and the frontmatter are byte-identical; `check-changeset-overwrite` reports the edit as a touched pre-existing changeset declaring the same packages, a deliberate correction.

## Open question for the seat

A data source that declares no `queryGroupHeaders` (the generic `ApiDataSource`, `ValueDataSource`, any host adapter) cannot give server-true counts. This PR keeps its old behaviour, grouping the fetched page, and keeps the `Partial` marker there because only there are the counts page slices, so the `grid.grouping.partial*` i18n rows are retained, not retired. The alternative is to refuse grouping loudly on such a source. Recommendation: keep, as done here. It is honest, it adds no code, and a refusal would break every grouped grid on a custom adapter with no server able to do better.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, measured: `POST /data/:object/query` with `groupBy` + `aggregations` + `search` answers the same five full-count groups as without `search`, while the same `search` on a flat query narrows to one row. The aggregate branch of `findData` composes `where` / `groupBy` / `aggregations` / `having` only, so the search is dropped silently. That is why `ListView` keeps hosting a searched grouped grid. Reported for filing in objectstack.
- `ListView` still issues its own window fetch for a grouped grid it hands over (it feeds the filter chips' option counts and the client export), so a grouped console view makes one extra request.
